subcategory: embedding-based context compression reusing retriever index embeddings (memory slots)
task: Open-domain question answering with compressed retrieved context
problem: Retrieved passages lengthen prompts and raise generator latency; embedding compressors either need a large ad-hoc compressor LLM (ICAE, PISCO) or collapse a passage to one projected vector (xRAG), losing lexical detail.
architecture: ConvX: a lightweight converter splits each indexed retriever embedding into M chunks and maps them, via a three-layer network with self-attention over slots, into a fixed number of memory slots in the LLM embedding space; slots are pretrained with vocabulary reconstruction, then the LLM is fine-tuned (LoRA, self-distillation) to answer from the slots; the converter is frozen so only it must be retrained for a new retriever.
retriever: SPLADE-v3 retrieval; passages re-encoded with the SFR retriever whose embeddings are converted
key_results: Average spanEM 0.508 at 16x compression and 0.505 at 128x vs 0.436 for xRAG (256x) and 0.542 for PISCO (16x); uncompressed RAG 0.589, no-context LLM 0.410.
Several compression baselines (AutoCompressor 0.329, ICAE 0.342) fall below the no-context lower bound.
strengths: Avoids double encoding by reusing index embeddings; competitive with an LLM-based compressor at much lower cost.
Releases passage collection, retrieved-passage dataset and checkpoint.

limitations.text: Not all memory slots carry informative vocabulary, leaving redundancy in the representation.
Evaluated only with the SFR retriever index; generalisation across retrievers is untested.
Still below PISCO and uncompressed RAG in average accuracy.

title: ConvX: A Lightweight Converter to Bridge Indexed Dense Representations and Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
